title: Truce of Vilna
text: The Truce of Vilna, Treaty of Wilno or Truce or Treaty of Niemieża was a treaty signed at Niemieża near Vilnius on 3 November 1656 between the Tsardom of Russia and Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, introducing a truce during the Russo-Polish War (1654–67) and an anti-Swedish alliance in the contemporaneous Second Northern War. In return for ceasing hostilities and fighting Sweden alongside Poland–Lithuania, the treaty promised tsar Alexis of Russia to succeed the Polish–Lithuanian throne as soon as John II Casimir Vasa would die. Thus began the Russo-Swedish War (1656–1658), which Russia would lose.
